design.title: Dashboard Date Filter & Statistics — by day, by month, custom range
design.summary: Add client-side date filtering to dashboard. Pill-style button bar (All/Today/7d/30d/Month/Custom) with month picker and date range inputs. filterByDate() applied before stats() so all widgets (stats cards, heatmap, trend chart, agent analysis, timeline) respect the selected period. ~120 lines in dashboard.html only. No backend changes.

newState.dateFilter: { mode: 'all' | 'today' | '7d' | '30d' | 'month' | 'custom', value?: string, from?: string, to?: string }

newFunctions.filterByDate(entries, df): Filters entries by date range based on dateFilter state, uses existing localDate() for timezone handling
newFunctions.updateFilterLabel(df, count): Shows human-readable label with run count when filter is active

design.integrationPoint: render() — insert filterByDate() call between entry collection and stats() call (line ~1770)

keyDecisions.client_side_only: Data volume is tiny (task executions). Entries already fully loaded. Zero backend risk.
keyDecisions.all_widgets_filtered: Date filter applied before stats() so stats cards, heatmap, trend, agents, timeline all see filtered data.
keyDecisions.composes_with_project_filter: Date filter at render() level, project filter inside renderTimeline(). Both compose correctly.
keyDecisions.dirty_check_update: Add dateFilter state to render key so filter changes trigger re-render.
keyDecisions.no_persistence: Filter resets to 'all' on page reload — simple, no localStorage needed.

implementationOrder: 2. HTML: Add filter bar between header and stats cards (~15 lines)
3. JS: Add dateFilter state variable + filterByDate() function
4. JS: Add button click handlers + input change handlers
5. JS: Integrate into render() — call filterByDate before stats()
6. JS: Update dirty-check key to include dateFilter state
7. JS: Add updateFilterLabel() for human-readable period display
8. Test: Verify all filter modes work, compose with project filter
